summary: Phase 149O.20L.7D.3 -- Action-6 File-Mode + Continuation-Baseline Proposition Amendment. Analysis + proposition amendment + human election + authorization publication only -- no Action 6 execution, no Actions 7-9 execution, no Actions 1-5 rerun, no Dell mutation, no DeploymentBinding, no certification, no activation. Independently reconstructed the immutable original Action-6 text from pinned commit f9e33232c83163aad5e50bc94db7cab51b844ac5 and the real 7D.2 failure evidence from commit 33f1dc0bae9c0fdba1bc792673ceb8193993734a. Finding D3-1: independently derived (not assumed) that the defect is a proposition (command-text) defect -- the frozen 'find -type f -exec chmod 0640' is unconditional and conflicts with its own clean-working-tree read-back for any repository tracking an executable file, which this one does (6 of 4030 tracked paths, full inventory enumerated: 4024x100644, 6x100755, 0 symlinks, 0 submodules). Reproduced the exact six-file, zero-content, mode-only defect in disposable local scratch (never Dell). Designed and validated the narrowest repair -- two 'find -perm -u+x' branches deterministically mapping Git index mode to filesystem mode (100644->0640, 100755->0750) -- with zero content diff, zero mode mismatch across all 4030 tracked paths, preserved hook/script executability, preserved non-executable semantics, and unchanged rollback, all in the same disposable scratch, disposed afterward. Finding D3-2: the retained Actions-1-5 baseline (independently reconfirmed unchanged and read-only this phase via live SSH to hac-dell) is conservatively bound as a fresh, explicit continuation precondition with its own read-only gates and STOP semantics, not silently treated as equivalent to the original absent-everything-host authorization; Action 2's existing principal is explicitly adjudicated as a required retained baseline, never a simulated fresh-creation state. Actions 7-9 independently determined unchanged. Finding D3-3: no canonical CHGR supersession/lifecycle-transition mechanism exists yet -- confirmed from primary source (governance_record_lifecycle_event.schema.json's own 'No transition command exists this increment' disclosure; governance-record publish has no linkage parameter) -- no mechanism was invented; precedence over chgr-96a0ce12756e4cc892492a87af1db832 established textually, and a dedicated future authority-model-repair phase is recommended. Presented the complete bounded amended proposition (docs/PHASE_149O_20L_7D_3_...md) to the human governance authority; recorded an explicit APPROVE election via the canonical pcae decision-session workflow (a first session, CDS-8984cecc..., hit the CHGR schema's 500-char decision_subject limit at publish time and was superseded by a shortened-subject re-run of the identical approval -- left Confirmed-but-unpublished as an honest evidentiary artifact, not deleted); separately confirmed the exact preview digest (a distinct step from selection, per governing instruction); published as new CHGR chgr-541cb08c313b4f8884970172d37c5a1d via the canonical governance-record publish path -- independently verified (outcome: verified). The prior CHGR chgr-96a0ce12756e4cc892492a87af1db832 remains byte-identical (digest unchanged, independently reverified) and untouched. Pinned source SHA, wrapper digest, and the HBDC-REQ-042 expected residual all reconfirmed unaffected by the repair. New, independently authored companion test module -- 31 tests combining live disposable-scratch reproduction/repair validation with static disclosure checks against the phase doc and the published CHGR -- re-run three consecutive times, 31 passed each run, no flake. No src/pcae/**, scripts/**, or docs/contracts/** file was modified. Recommends exactly one next phase: 149O.20L.7D.4 -- independent verification of this amendment before any execution retry. Does not recommend 149O.20L.7D.5 directly, since execution has not yet occurred. No certification. No activation. Stops here.
